title: Animal life stages
keyIdea: Animals, including humans, have young that grow into adults. People grow through life stages in one order: baby, child, teenager, adult and older adult. A kitten grows into a cat and a puppy into a dog: young grow into the same kind of animal as their parents and look like them, but not exactly. Different animals take different times to grow up: a mouse in about 2 months, a dog in 1 to 2 years and a person in about 18 years.
familyTip: Look at family photos together and put them in order from youngest to oldest: who was a baby, who is a teenager now, who is an older adult? Ask your child what changed in their own photos (height, teeth, hair) and what stayed the same.

visual.caption: Young animal or grown-up? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: grow a person along an age line, order the stages, grow kittens into cats, race a mouse, dog and child, and sort what changes.

kid: All animals have babies. People do too. The babies grow up and become adults.
A person grows in stages. First a baby, then a child, then a teenager. Next comes an adult, and last an older adult. The stages go one way. You can not grow back into a baby.
A kitten grows into a cat. A puppy grows into a dog. The young look like their mum and dad, but not exactly the same.
Some animals grow up fast. A mouse is grown up in about 2 months. A dog takes about 1 or 2 years. A person takes about 18 years.
adult: Ages 6 to 7. This is the Year 2 statutory aim in the National Curriculum in England: notice that animals, including humans, have offspring which grow into adults. It also matches NGSS 1-LS3-1, young animals are like, but not exactly like, their parents. Key words: offspring, young, adult, grow, life stage, baby, child, teenager, older adult.

Growing up happens in stages over time. Humans grow from baby to adult over about 18 years, and adults stop growing taller. Many young animals have their own names, such as kitten, puppy, calf and lamb. Some, like frogs and butterflies, look very different from their parents at first; that is the Year 2 life-cycle idea.

Common mistakes: thinking babies stay babies, or that a young animal could grow into a different animal; thinking older people can turn back into babies; skipping the teenage stage; and thinking all animals take as long as people to grow up. Children may also expect offspring to look exactly like one parent.

In the lab your child drags a person along an age line from 0 to 80, puts five stages in order and grows three kittens into cats with their own coats. Then they move time on to watch a mouse, a dog and a child grow up, and sort what changes as we grow.

practice.prompt: Which life stage comes after teenager?
practice.hint: The stages go: baby, child, teenager, then …
practice.explain: After teenager comes adult. The order is baby, child, teenager, adult, older adult.

practice.prompt: What does a calf grow into?
practice.hint: A calf drinks milk from its mum, a cow.
practice.explain: A calf is a young cow, so it grows into a cow, like its parents.

practice.prompt: Mia is {a} years old. A person is grown up at about 18. About how many more years until Mia is grown up?
practice.hint: Count on from Mia's age to 18.
practice.explain: 18 − {a} = {=18-a}. Mia will be grown up in about {=18-a} years.

practice.prompt: A cat had {k} kittens, and a dog had {p} puppies. How many young animals is that?
practice.hint: Add the kittens and the puppies.
practice.explain: {k} + {p} = {=k+p} young animals. The kittens will grow into cats and the puppies into dogs.

practice.hint: Small animals like mice grow up in a few weeks.
practice.explain: A mouse is grown up in about 2 months. People take about 18 years, and elephants more than 10 years.

pool.prompt: What do all animals, including people, have that grow into adults?
pool.hint: Think of a kitten, a lamb and a baby.
pool.explain: All animals have young, and the young grow into adults.

pool.prompt: What is the first life stage of a person?
pool.explain: Everyone starts as a baby, then grows into a child.

pool.prompt: Can an older adult grow back into a child?
choices: No, the stages go one way
Yes, when they are very old
pool.hint: Do the stages ever go backwards?
pool.explain: Life stages only go one way: baby, child, teenager, adult, older adult.

pool.prompt: A ginger cat and a black cat have kittens. What will the kittens grow into?
choices: Cats that look a bit like their parents
Exactly the same cat as mum
pool.hint: Young are like their parents, but not exactly the same.
pool.explain: The kittens grow into cats. Each looks a bit like its mum and dad, but not exactly the same.

pool.prompt: A puppy is {m} months old. It is grown up at about 18 months. How many more months is that?
pool.hint: Take the puppy's age away from 18.
pool.explain: 18 − {m} = {=18-m} more months until the dog is grown up.
15 is between 13 and 19, so a 15-year-old is a teenager.

pool.prompt: What changes as a child grows into an adult?
pool.hint: Think of what stays the same and what changes.
pool.explain: A child gets taller, but stays a human with the same number of eyes.

pool.prompt: A hen has {c} chicks. {g} have grown into hens. How many are still chicks?
pool.hint: Take the grown-up ones away from all the chicks.
pool.explain: {c} − {g} = {=c-g} are still chicks. They will grow into hens too.

pool.prompt: What is a young sheep called?
pool.hint: Young sheep are born in spring on farms.
pool.explain: A young sheep is a lamb. It grows into a sheep, like its parents.
